title: 1958 AHSME Problem 16
statement: The area of a circle inscribed in a regular hexagon is \(100\pi.\) The area of the hexagon is:

solutions.text:
The circle has radius \(r=10,\) which is the hexagon’s apothem. Thus the side length is \[ 2r\tan30^\circ=\frac{20}{\sqrt3}. \] Using one-half the product of perimeter and apothem, the hexagon’s area is \[ \frac12\left(6\cdot\frac{20}{\sqrt3}\right)(10) =200\sqrt3. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The circle’s radius is the apothem of the regular hexagon
For apothem \(r,\) the hexagon side is \(2r\tan30^\circ\)
